NutriCorp Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline, or click the Q&A button in the webcast interface if you're online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Elena Vargas, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: EBITDA margin performance and key factors; key achievements and challenges in the quarter; impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue; volume and price/mix analysis; EPS guidance and key assumptions; and organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year.

Overall, these areas highlight our operational resilience and strategic progress in beverages, snacks, and plant-based nutritionals. We're executing our playbook effectively—balancing pricing discipline with productivity gains, navigating FX volatility, and leaning into premium health trends. Key achievements included robust organic top-line growth and margin expansion, even as we tackled commodity inflation and supply disruptions. Challenges like labor tightness and regulatory hurdles in EMEA were met head-on with targeted mitigations.

We're confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $1.62 billion, representing a 1% increase on a reported basis and 5.2% organically year-over-year, excluding a 4.2 percentage point FX headwind. Gross margin expanded 320 basis points to 32.4%, reflecting pricing actions and cost savings that offset input pressures. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $285 million, or 17.6%, up 210 basis points. Operating income was $240 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.25, up 8% organically.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We repurchased $150 million in shares this quarter under our $2 billion authorization and raised our quarterly dividend by 5%. We're committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Let me dive deeper into those six areas Mike highlighted, starting with our EBITDA margin performance and the key factors driving it. This continues to underscore the strength of our operational playbook in this dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. For the quarter, we delivered that $285 million in adjusted EBITDA on $1.62 billion in revenue, translating to 17.6%—a robust 210 basis point expansion year-over-year. Through the first three quarters, our EBITDA margin is 16.8%, up 150 basis points from last year, putting us at the high end of peers like PepsiCo's core F&B segments around 18% or Mondelez's 17-19% range, despite commodity inflation and FX volatility.

This isn't by chance—it's from disciplined execution on pricing, cost productivity, and portfolio mix shifts. On gross margins, that 320 basis point expansion to 32.4% was the main driver. Organic revenue grew 5.2%, with 6.8% from price/mix more than offsetting a 1.6% volume dip, even as global food CPI hovers at 8-10% per FAO data. We've passed through about 85% of input inflation via targeted pricing, amid cocoa up 40% YTD from West African constraints and dairy/sugar adding 15-20%—pressures Hershey and General Mills have echoed.

Pricing is complemented by $42 million in quarterly productivity savings, aiming for 4-5% of COGS annually. We've rolled out SAP S/4HANA across 70% of North American plants for 12% procurement savings via AI forecasting and supplier auctions, similar to Nestlé's Project Magnify but fit for our snacks and ready-to-drink lines. Our sugarcane hedging covers 80% for FY25 at $0.18 per pound, dodging Brazil drought risks, while a 15% stake in a Midwest dairy co-op stabilized cream costs against 25% Q2 spikes. In Mexico City, robotic palletizers and IoT sensors boosted throughput 18% and cut labor variances 22%, part of our $150 million CAPEX for 2% annual yield gains across 45 plants. These offset a $28 million input headwind—commodities are 55% of COGS—and protected against 100-150 basis point compression.

SG&A deleveraged 110 basis points to 14.8% of sales, adding over half the EBITDA lift, via $18 million in zero-based budgeting and shared services, keeping G&A flat despite 7% R&D headcount growth for plant-based work. Marketing shifted 15% to digital platforms like NielsenIQ and Circana for high-ROI amid softening demand.

By segment: Beverages, 52% of revenue, saw EBITDA margins up 280 basis points to 20.1% from premiumization in functional waters like HydraBoost, up 22% with 25% pricing premiums—volumes steady as 62% of consumers seek low-cal per Mintel, favoring us over sugary rivals. Snacks & Convenience, 48%, expanded 150 basis points to 14.9%, with savory snacks up 9% organically and air-fried potatoes offsetting cocoa hits, plus private label wins at Kroger and Walmart.

Regionally, North America (65%) hit 19.2% margins, up 250 basis points, via pricing and 3% club channel volume. EMEA (20%) dipped to 13.5% on energy surcharges post-Ukraine and EU Deforestation costs, mitigated by Turkish pistachios over California imports—Q4 recovery expected. APAC/LATAM (15%) reached 16.8%, up 300 basis points, on 12% Indonesia/Brazil RTD tea growth, with e-commerce at 18% vs. 12% global.

Forward, we see 16.5-17.5% full-year EBITDA margins, Q4 up another 100 basis points, via portfolio tweaks like divesting low-margin dairy for $120 million to fund alt-protein bars targeting 20%+ margins; sustainability unlocking regenerative ag for 10% input stability and Gen Z appeal; and $45 million R&D for 15 SKUs like fiber-fortified drinks in the $50 billion gut health market by 2027.

Next, on key achievements and challenges this quarter. We posted net sales of $1.62 billion, up 5.2% organically excluding our HealthySip acquisition—our strongest in three years, with 1.8% volume growth across beverages, snacks, and plant-based. Beverages' NutriGlow electrolytes surged 14% on 2,500 new convenience stores and TikTok Gen Z campaigns. Snacks grew 4% organically, gaining 1.2 share points in U.S. savory per Nielsen via low-sodium chips.

North America (62%) rose 11% organically, taking premium hydration share from PepsiCo's Propel. Asia-Pacific jumped 25% via Indonesia JV with IndoFood on RTD teas. EMEA grew 3%, offset by Middle East halal nuts. Gross margins expanded 220 basis points to 32.4% via 5-7% pricing and AI hedging locking corn/sugar 15% below spot, shielding cocoa rallies like Hershey's. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to $285 million at 17.6%, from $50 million supply chain savings including 20% ocean freight cuts post-Panama expansion.

Operationally, SAP S/4HANA covers 80% of plants, cutting working capital 12 days; Blue Yonder AI forecasting hit 92% accuracy, slashing stockouts 30%; 75% beverage packaging now rPET, lifting ESG to 85/100 on Sustainalytics for Walmart priority.

Challenges included 12% dairy and 18% edible oil inflation per USDA, compressing plant-based margins 100 basis points—mitigated by pea protein swaps. Midwest labor turnover at 18% added $15 million in temps/training, like Tyson. Value segment softened 3% to private labels per IRI; UK HFSS reforms delayed savory launches $10 million; Brazil El Niño spiked robusta 25% for RTD coffee; Coca-Cola pricing eroded 0.5 share in protein shakes. We're upping R&D to $120 million for monk fruit sodas, with e-commerce at 18% driving 30% growth; Q4 organic at 6-8%, margins 32.4%.

Turning to FX impact on revenue. Reported Q3 revenue up 1% to $1.62 billion, but constant currency grew 5.2%. FX headwind was $68 million or 4.2 percentage points, third straight quarter of USD strength (7% trade-weighted YTD), like PepsiCo/Mondelez 3-5% drags.

Europe (22%, EuroCrisp snacks, Sparkle beverages) had $28 million hit from 6.2% euro drop, plus Germany/France inflation softness. UK sterling offset at -2.1%. LatAm (18%, Agave drinks, fruit snacks) $24 million from Brazil real -8.4% and Mexico peso -5.7%, but local grew 9.1%. APAC (12%) $16 million from India rupee -4.9% and yuan slowdown.

Mitigations: 65% hedge on 2025 exposures with 15-month forwards/collars at LIBOR+50bps, better than Coke's shorter tenors; 72% LatAm COGS local via JBS; dynamic pricing in 14 markets adding 2.3 points. New plants in Indonesia/Poland/Colombia by Q2 2025 localize 85% production, neutralizing 1-2% swings; Middle East halal up 15%. Q4 FX $50-60 million, full-year ~$225 million; constant currency 5-7% organic.

On volume and price/mix: Organic growth 5.2% split +1.8% volume, +4.4% price/mix—third quarter price/mix leading amid inflation, volumes resilient.

Beverages (42%): +2.1% volume ahead IRI 0.8%, AquaSparkle Zero +12% on convenience/distribution and campaigns; price/mix +5.2% (ASP +3.8% on CSDs 4-6%, mix +1.4% premium hydration like VitaQuench +18%). Snacks (35%): volume +0.1%, NutriCrunch +22% plant-based; price/mix +4.1% (ASP +3.2% on potatoes/oils, mix +0.9% BFY 28%). Dairy/Alternatives (23%): volume +3.5% vs. Rabobank 1.2%, OatGlow +14%; price/mix +4.0% (ASP +2.9%, mix +1.1% Greek).

North America (55%): volume +1.5%, price/mix +5.1%. EMEA +2.4% volume, +3.8% price/mix tempered by HFSS. LatAm +4.2% volume, APAC -0.5% but +4.6% price/mix. SymphonyAI elasticity modeling improved realization 150bps; discontinued 12 SKUs for high-NMV. Pillars: $250M for RTD lines targeting 5% H2 volume; BFY to 35% by FY25; 70% hedges. Q3 organic 5-7%, volume +2-3%, price/mix +3-4%.

For EPS guidance: Q3 adjusted EPS $1.25, +8% organic, beating by $0.03 on snacks pricing and hydration mix.

Full-year FY2024 raised to $4.80-$4.95 (Q4 $1.40-$1.50, +12-20%), midpoint +7%. Organic revenue 6-7% (Q4 5-6%): pricing +4-5%, volume/mix +1-2%; zero-sugar CSDs +15%, RTD teas double-digit APAC, KettleFire nuts +200bps vs. Frito-Lay. NA 5-6% premium hydration/e-com 18%; EMEA 7-8% OatFlex; APAC 8-9%; LatAm 4-5%. Gross margin +120bps to 42.0% (Q4 42.5%), inflation 2.5-3.5% hedged (sugar +2%, cocoa +10%/4% COGS); $150M resiliency adds 75bps, rPET 50bps. SG&A 21.5% flat, $40M savings; op margin +80bps to 20.5%. Interest $220M, tax 23.5%, shares 420M, $300M buybacks. FX neutral, 10% stronger USD -2 cents.

'Vitality 2025': premium to 30%, digital analytics, $1.5B M&A; hedges buffer cocoa/tariffs.

Finally, organic sales growth guidance: Q3 actual 5.2% beat 3-5%, +2.1% pricing Snacks/Beverages offsetting cocoa/sugar/dairy, +2.8% volume/mix NutriFit/ZeroSugar; NA snacking +10bps share vs. 3.1% category.

Q4: 4-6%. Beverages 5-7% (RTD NutriBrew +6% volume, +2.5 share $12B category); Snacks 3-5% (+3% volume plant-based VeggieCrunch +15%); Convenience 4-6% e-com 12%. NA 5-7% premium 35%; Europe 2-4% FX/reg; EM 6-8% Brazil/APAC. Drivers: 1-2% pricing AI POS; 3% volume 15 SKUs/distribution/loyalty; Farm-to-Fork hedges cocoa $4,200/ton, Mexico nearshoring -15% costs. E-com 18% to 25%, snacking +10%, functionals. Full-year raised to 5-7%, innovation/share vs. flat industry.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS $4.80-$4.95 and organic growth 5-7%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Alex Rivera (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, Alex. Inflation remains elevated but manageable. As Lisa detailed, we've passed 85% through pricing while layering $42 million in productivity—supply chain digitization, hedging, automation—offsetting cocoa, dairy, and oils. Gross margins expanded significantly, and we're hedged into FY25. Our premium mix and BFY focus give us pricing power without volume erosion, unlike peers seeing bigger contractions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jamie Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Jamie Lee (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for the new plant-based beverage line and what is the expected contribution to growth?

Raj Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Jamie. Our new fiber-fortified, gut-health plant-based beverages—like extensions of HydraBoost and OatGlow—are central to our innovation pipeline, with $45 million R&D yielding 15 SKUs this year. Launching Q4 in NA and APAC, targeting the $50 billion gut health market by 2027. Early tests show 20% trial rates via e-comm and club channels; expect 1-2 points to Q4 organic growth, scaling to 30% of beverages portfolio by FY26, driving double-digit category velocity like Pepsi Zero's ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Chris Patel (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Elena Vargas (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, Chris. Disruptions from weather, El Niño, and geopolitics persist, but our resiliency program is delivering. SAP/Blue Yonder for 92% forecast accuracy cut stockouts 30%; nearshoring Mexico reroutes save 15-20% freight; regenerative ag and local sourcing like Turkish pistachios/JBS stabilize 72% LatAm COGS. New plants localize production; we're ahead on cocoa hedges at $4,200/ton vs. $6,500 spot. This saved $50 million this year, positioning Q4 volumes +2-3%.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Taylor Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Taylor Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Taylor, Q4 looks solid with organic 4-6%, EPS $1.40-$1.50, margins expanding. Momentum in premium hydration/snacks, innovation ramps, distribution gains offset any macro softening. Constant currency growth 5-7%, FX ~$50-60 million headwind assumed. We're executing Vitality 2025—premium to 30%, e-com 25%, M&A—with strong FCF for buybacks/dividends. Confident in outperformance.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
